+    Repeatable failure (direct bundle runs with `swiftpm-testing-helper ... --filter aChunkThatSettlesAParagraphEvaluatesOnlyTheNewParagraph`, each run a new process):
+    - 50 new processes one after the other: 13 failed. 60 new processes, 6 in parallel: 43 failed. 60 new processes, 12 in parallel: 0 to 27 failed for each batch, by machine load (load average 30 to 50).

+    - `aLongStreamNeverEvaluatesASettledParagraphAgain`: 0 of 120 under the same load. That test starts with no settled paragraph.
+
+    Cause (temporary `_printChanges` and `==` prints, now removed):
+    - In a failing case, `==` of `ParagraphView` is NOT called. SwiftUI evaluates the body with "@self changed".
+    - Before the chunk, SwiftUI reports `ResponseView: _theme changed` and `SettledParagraphs: @self, _theme changed`. A probe view that reads the same `\.agentTheme` at the same place did not evaluate again. Thus the theme value did not change: SwiftUI cannot show that the `AgentTheme` value is equal when the environment of the hosting view changes after the mount, and it reports a change. The pending update of the settled paragraph then evaluates its body with the chunk, with no Equatable check.
+    - In passing cases, this theme update did not occur, or it occurred before the first pump ended.
+    - Experiment: the two views read a constant theme instead of `@Environment(\.agentTheme)`: 0 of 180 failures under the same load, and no extra evaluation in the logs.
+    - An extra 50 ms pump, a read of the accessibility tree, or `layoutSubtreeIfNeeded` before the reset did not remove the failure.
+
+    The cause is in kit code: `ResponseView` and `SettledParagraphs` read the full `AgentTheme` from the environment, but they use only `spacing.m`. Plan: read only that CGFloat with `@Environment(\.agentTheme.spacing.m)`, so that SwiftUI compares a plain number.

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m4bbjg2kzg4n5vy8stvnkmek
+  text: |-
+    Correction to the earlier research comment, and the real cause.
+
+    What did not work:
+    - `@Environment(\.agentTheme.spacing.m)` in `ResponseView` and `SettledParagraphs` (instead of the full theme): after this change SwiftUI reported no theme change, but the test still failed in 115 of 410 new processes. The theme report was a side effect, not the cause. The earlier 0 of 180 result with a constant theme was a low-failure period. That change is reverted.
+    - A test with a root environment change (a custom environment key, or a dark window appearance) before or with the chunk did not fail. Thus there is no repeatable unit test for the cause other than the existing test in new processes.
+
+    Discriminating experiments (each 360 test cases, 12 processes in parallel, load average 37 to 46):
+    - No warm-up: 54 failures. A tail-only chunk before the measured chunk: 38 failures. A chunk that settles a paragraph before the measured chunk: 0 failures. Thus the first change of the paragraph list after the mount evaluates a paragraph that was there at the mount.
+    - `ParagraphView` with no `@Environment` property (temporary constant group): 0 of 360.
+
+    Cause, in kit code: `ParagraphView` had `@Environment(\.accessibilityMessageGroupID)`. A view with an environment property can evaluate its body on the first change of the `ForEach` data after the mount, and SwiftUI does not call `==` first (the temporary `==` print showed no call in each failing case). The paragraph splitter is correct: the paragraph values were equal.
+
+    Fix:
+    - `ParagraphView` has no environment property now. It stores `readingGroupID: String`, and `==` compares it. The public `init(messageID:paragraph:readingGroupID:)` has a new defaulted argument (`nil` uses the group of the message id), so that a caller outside the kit can give the group.
+    - `ParagraphList` (in `ResponseView.swift`) reads `accessibilityMessageGroupID` from the environment and gives the group to each paragraph. The reading group behaviour is the same.
+    - New unit test `ResponseViewHostedTests.twoParagraphViewsInDifferentReadingGroupsAreNotEqual`.
